findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in backfill_from_managed_refs that a backfill record is written ONLY when no record already exists for the key (skip keys already carrying push/snapshot/backfill), so backfill can never downgrade a push record written earlier in the same pass by _apply_mutations.
evidence: Plan Scope: 'write a record keyed (ticket_local_id, target, kind) with source="backfill"' — no never-downgrade / write-if-absent condition stated
AC5: 'a backfill never overwrites an existing "push" or "snapshot" record (provenance upgrades, never downgrades)'
peer_confirmations.py:150-164 record() unconditionally reassigns self._records[key]
reconcile.py:203-204 _apply_mutations (which triggers handle_update push records via apply_handlers.py:226-235) runs before _persist_and_log where backfill is invoked
findings.finding: The backfill mechanism as specified will DOWNGRADE existing provenance, contradicting its own AC5. backfill_from_managed_refs is told to 'write a record ... with source="backfill"' with no guard, but PeerConfirmationStore.record() overwrites unconditionally. On a fresh-upgrade pass, handle_update writes source="push" records during _apply_mutations (reconcile.py:203) BEFORE backfill runs in _persist_and_log (reconcile.py:204). Backfill would overwrite those push records with source="backfill".
scenarios: First post-upgrade pass that also performs an outbound link push: the pushed link gets a source="push" record during apply, then backfill clobbers it to source="backfill", weakening provenance and failing AC5
findings.suggested_fix: State that backfill consults store.get(...) (or is_confirmed) per key and writes only when absent — never overwriting an existing record — which satisfies AC5's no-downgrade half directly and leaves the snapshot upgrade (S2, running after backfill) to overwrite backfill records.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the backfill_from_managed_refs scope the explicit guard that skips writing when store.get(...) already holds a push- or snapshot-sourced record, since record() itself overwrites unconditionally and cannot provide AC5's no-downgrade behavior.
evidence: AC5: 'a backfill never overwrites an existing "push" or "snapshot" record (provenance upgrades, never downgrades)'
peer_confirmations.py record() lines 150-164 unconditionally does self._records[key] = {... 'source': source_kind ...} with no provenance guard
Scope says only: 'write a record keyed (ticket_local_id, target, kind) with source="backfill"...' — no skip-if-existing-push/snapshot guard
findings.finding: AC5's 'backfill never overwrites an existing push or snapshot record' is refuted by the actual record() and unspecified in the backfill scope, which describes an unconditional write.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC5 / Scope backfill_from_managed_refs bullet
scenarios: A backfill pass runs over a key that already carries a push/snapshot record and clobbers it down to source=backfill, contradicting AC5's no-downgrade half
findings.suggested_fix: In backfill_from_managed_refs, before recording, consult store.get(source,target,kind) and skip when its 'source' is SOURCE_PUSH or SOURCE_SNAPSHOT; only write when absent.
